learnings.question: Which 19th-century researcher demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed in the 1880s that we forget about 80% of what we learn within 24 hours unless we actively force ourselves to recall it — the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term do researchers use for the phenomenon where writing something down or saving it digitally causes the brain to feel it no longer needs to remember it?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the "Google Effect" paper call this Digital Amnesia — the moment we write something down or store it digitally, our brains treat it as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In agile project management, what is the name of the chart that visualizes a team's remaining work during a sprint and helps track whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: A Burndown Chart is a Scrum artifact that visualizes the progress of a Sprint, showing remaining work and helping the team track whether it's on schedule.

learnings.question: What is the primary purpose of breaking a software development process into short, iterative cycles known as Sprints?
options: To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To increase the length of the project
To eliminate the need for testing
To reduce the number of team members needed
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a project into short, iterative cycles called Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments than a single long development cycle would.

learnings.question: What Arabic term refers to a mindful awareness of God's presence that fosters self-restraint and purifies one's intentions?
learnings.learning: Taqwa describes an awareness of Allah's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies intentions, guiding a person away from wrongdoing.

learnings.question: Which phrase did Prophet Muhammad reportedly say to model an attitude of gratitude toward God?
options: Shall I not be a grateful servant?
Shall I not be a humble servant?
Shall I not be a faithful servant?
Shall I not be a patient servant?
learnings.learning: Prophet Muhammad modeled gratitude by asking, "Shall I not be a grateful servant?" (Sahih Bukhari 1130), framing gratitude as central to worship.

learnings.question: According to Islamic teaching, what did Prophet Muhammad say would follow him instead of further prophethood?
learnings.learning: Prophet Muhammad said, "There will be no prophet after me; instead, there will be caliphs" (Sahih Bukhari 3455), tying the concept of khalifah to collective responsibility for the faith.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents the deepest power-saving mode, where the device is almost completely powered down and takes the longest time to resume activity?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state — the device is almost completely powered down, used for the longest periods of inactivity, giving the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In an analogy comparing PCIe power states to everyday computer behavior, which power state is compared to a computer screen turning off — less active, but able to quickly resume full operation?
learnings.learning: L0s is described as similar to a computer screen turning off: a light sleep state designed for very short idle periods, able to quickly wake and resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, as shaped by their own actions and decisions?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in life, shaped by our actions and decisions, distinct from Qadr, which is Allah's complete eternal plan.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: According to a verse from Surah Ar-Ra'd cited in Islamic teaching, what must happen before a person's condition or circumstances will change?
options: Allah must be asked three times
The person must change what is within themselves
A scholar must issue a ruling
A full lunar year must pass
learnings.learning: "Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves" (Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11) frames personal change as the trigger for changed circumstances.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: What potential misunderstanding does the concept of Qadr address regarding a person changing their circumstances through sincere supplication (Dua)?
options: That Qada' cannot be influenced by human action at all
That supplication is unnecessary since everything is predetermined
That only prophets' prayers can be answered
That such a change would be something Allah did not already know or plan for
learnings.learning: Even when Dua changes a person's Qada' (life outcome), that very change was always known to Allah and is already part of His Qadr — the two are not in tension.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: Roughly how many distinct words exist in Arabic compared to the roughly 170,000 words catalogued in the Oxford English Dictionary?
learnings.learning: Arabic has around 12 million distinct words versus about 170,000 in the Oxford English Dictionary — roughly a 71:1 ratio — a key reason a Quran word-frequency analysis used the original Arabic text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: When a data analysis applied the 80/20 Pareto Principle to word frequency in the Quran, what percentage of the text did the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Contrary to the Pareto Principle's 80/20 expectation, the top 20 most frequent words in the Quran only account for about 20.83% of the text, not 80%.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is 'Tashkeel,' a factor that posed a data-analysis challenge in a study of word frequency in the Quran's original Arabic text?
options: A classification of Quranic chapters by theme
A method of translating Arabic into English
Diacritical marks that indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings above or below Arabic letters indicating vowel sounds; the analysis used text without them, trading some precision for a simpler, more uniform dataset.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
